title: Accessing and Slicing Python Tuples
learningObjectives: Explain the behavior of accessing and slicing python tuples.
Use tuple operations to represent and process fixed sequences.
Predict the result of indexing, unpacking or combining tuples.
Distinguish immutable tuple operations from mutable list operations.
Apply tuples to a small data-processing task.

understand.concept: Tuple indexing and slicing work like list indexing and slicing. Indexes start at zero; negative indexes count from the end. Slices use an exclusive stop boundary and return a new tuple. Attempting to access an invalid individual index raises IndexError.
understand.whyItMatters: Indexing and slicing retrieve individual tuple values or selected groups without changing the original tuple.
understand.analogy: It is like reading a position or a section from a fixed sequence card.
understand.analogyLimit: A slice creates a new tuple containing references to the selected objects; it does not deep-copy nested objects.

explain.narrative:
## 1. Positive and negative indexes

Use `values[0]` for the first item and `values[-1]` for the last.

## 2. Slicing

Use `values[start:stop:step]`. The stop value is excluded.

## 3. Reverse a tuple

A negative step such as `[::-1]` returns a reversed tuple.

## 4. Index errors

An invalid individual index raises IndexError.

examples.title: Access first and last
examples.explanation: Positive zero selects the first item; negative one selects the last.

examples.title: Access a middle item
examples.explanation: The third item has index two.

examples.title: Slice a tuple
examples.explanation: The slice includes index one and excludes index four.

examples.title: Use a slice step
examples.explanation: A step of two selects every second tuple item.

examples.title: Reverse a tuple
examples.explanation: A negative step returns a new tuple in reverse order.

practise.guidedTask: Access the first and last values and create a middle slice from a tuple of at least five items.
practise.independentTask: Given a tuple of ten values, extract the first three, last three and every second item. Explain why the original tuple remains unchanged.
hints: A slice excludes its stop index.
Indexing outside the tuple raises IndexError.
practise.challenge: Predict tuple slices using omitted boundaries and negative steps. Explain the type of each slice result.

questions.prompt: What is the index of the first tuple item?

questions.explanation: Negative one refers to the final tuple element.

questions.prompt: Is a tuple slice stop index included?

options: The original tuple unchanged in forward order
questions.explanation: A negative step traverses the tuple backwards.

questions.prompt: What error occurs for an invalid individual index?
questions.explanation: An out-of-range tuple index raises IndexError.
